sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture and Aseptic Tubing of Ambient Quick-Cook Tapioca Pearls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Taiwan (source jurisdiction of the Taiwanese non-resident investor; the WFOE will be incorporated in the People's Republic of China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - PRC civil-law/socialist statutory system governs the WFOE, while Taiwan-origin corporate documents are prepared under Taiwan's civil-law framework and must pass cross-strait authentication
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: No formal inter-state BIT or DTAA applies because Taiwan is not a separate sovereign under PRC law; the following cross-strait agreements are the operative investment-protection instruments
Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA, effective September 12, 2010)
Cross-Strait Agreement on Investment Protection and Promotion (effective February 1, 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Legal Persons and Other Organizations (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective November 1, 2024); Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective July 1, 2024); Provisions of the State Administration for Market Regulation on Enterprise Name Registration and Administration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Commercial One-Stop Company Registration Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille is not available because Taiwan is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; PRC consular legalization is also not available for Taiwan-origin corporate records; the mandatory route is Taiwan notary public notarization, Taiwan district court/notary office certification, Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) verification, then Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) counterpart verification and acceptance by the PRC provincial notary association or SAMR.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or current Company Registration Status Certificate of the Taiwan investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company Registration Records Division
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan notary public authentication of the registry-extracted status certificate, followed by Taiwan court/notary office certification, SEF verification, ARATS verification, and acceptance by the PRC authority; no Hague Apostille and no consular legalization chain applies.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation of the PRC WFOE and opening of PRC bank accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or shareholders meeting of the Taiwan investing company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The resolution or Power of Attorney must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public, certified by the Taiwan district court, verified by SEF, transmitted through ARATS, and then accepted by the PRC SAMR and bank; Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and neither applies here.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum of Association of the Taiwan investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) certified filing copy or the investor company's registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy of the Taiwan-registered Articles of Association must be notarized in Taiwan, certified by the competent Taiwan court/notary office, verified by SEF, sent through ARATS, and then used in the PRC; this is a standalone cross-strait legalization path, not a consular legalization or Apostille procedure.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued for the Taiwan investor company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan commercial bank maintaining the investor's operating and settlement accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be notarized as to the authorized bank signatory's execution and bank seal in Taiwan, certified by the Taiwan court/notary office, verified by SEF, forwarded through ARATS to the PRC counterpart, and then presented to the PRC bank/tax authority; no Hague Apostille and no consular legalization route is used.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the PRC counsel and the Taiwan investor must complete evidence-based CDD/KYC on all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorized signatories. Screening must cover the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN/SSI and consolidated non-SDN lists, the PRC domestic sanctions and unreliable entity lists, and Taiwan/SAMR adverse records. PEP identification must include domestic and foreign prominent public functionaries, their family members and close associates, with enhanced scrutiny of source of wealth and source of funds. UBOs holding at least 25% direct or indirect equity must be declared to the SAMR/PBOC beneficial-owner database under Government_Only_Access, and any nominee arrangements must be documented and disclosed to the bank to avoid shell-company red flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Enterprise Name Registration and Reservation System, integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (www.gsxt.gov.cn) and the National Government Service Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered WFOE name must be in simplified Chinese characters and must follow the mandatory four-tier composition: administrative division + distinctive name + industry or business scope + organizational form ('limited liability company'). Traditional Chinese characters and pinyin romanization sourced from the Taiwan investor may only inspire phonetic transliteration in the distinctive element; the English name is not a registered legal name. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing PRC-registered name, a well-known mark, or a protected public institution name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must first request the written SAMR rejection reason. Within 60 days of receipt, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration with the market regulation administration at the next higher level under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, or file an administrative lawsuit with the competent people's court within six months under the Administrative Litigation Law. Before or during the appeal, the applicant may also re-submit a corrected name through the online SAMR name-reservation portal by adding a more distinctive element, removing prohibited/sensitive tokens, and attaching evidence of trademark rights, prior trade name use, or consent letters. The reservation window is 30 days; if extension is locally available, apply once before expiry; after expiry the name must be re-reserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this industry. Under the PRC Food Safety Law and the Administrative Measures for Food Production Licensing, a canned boba tapioca pearls manufacturing WFOE must hold a Food Production License (SC license) and must possess fixed, lawful production premises, food-safety facilities, cleaner production areas, equipment, and utility connections. A virtual office, commercial mailbox, or incubator address cannot satisfy the mandatory pre-licensing factory inspection by local SAMR. Tax authorities require the registered address to match the actual operational address for VAT invoice quota and tax registration, and PRC banks reject virtual-office addresses during on-site verification for RMB basic deposit account opening. Therefore, a physical industrial/food-grade lease must be secured before incorporation; a virtual office may only be considered for a non-manufacturing auxiliary back-office, never for the registered production address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) mandatory Food Production License technical review and site inspection by local SAMR before issuance; (2) SAMR 'dual random' unannounced food-safety compliance inspection within the first 12-24 months of operation; (3) tax bureau field verification for a newly established food manufacturer requesting normal or elevated VAT invoice limits; (4) fire protection and environmental protection inspections before commencement of production; (5) customs or export food-facility verification if the WFOE later exports canned boba pearls. Quantified risk: high, approximately 70% probability of at least one unannounced physical inspection within the first 18 months after the start of operations, and a 100% probability of a pre-license physical factory inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government registration of WFOE company name and issuance of business license (official administrative fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation and local municipal Market Regulation Bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory tariff; PRC enterprise registration administrative fees have been abolished; only incidental local e-stamp or document printing charges may apply

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Food Production License (SC) application and technical review administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Market Regulation Bureau / SAMR food safety authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No administrative filing fee under PRC Food Safety Law; applicant bears third-party expert review, product testing, and premises modification costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Taiwan investor Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, Board Resolution, Articles of Association and Bank Reference Letter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan notary public and Taiwan district court/notary office certification authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Taiwan notary tariff schedule; prevailing package rate for a five-document corporate notarization set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-strait document verification and forwarding through SEF and ARATS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and mainland provincial ARATS verification body
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Published SEF/ARATS document verification and forwarding fee schedule; per-document and per-delivery charges

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese translation of Taiwan corporate documents and bank records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of approximately USD 80-120 per 1,000 translated Chinese characters

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank reference letter issuance and notary certification of bank signatory by the Taiwan issuing bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Taiwan issuing bank and Taiwan notary office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Taiwan commercial bank corporate service charge for reference letters plus notary certification of authorized signatory

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO information filing, AML/KYC preparation, and beneficial-owner documentation package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained licensed PRC corporate compliance or legal service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No PBOC/SAMR government filing fee applies; this is the prevailing professional service fee for preparing and filing the beneficial-owner information return under Order No. 3

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence, name clearance support, lease review, and WFOE incorporation counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained PRC law firm with foreign investment and food-manufacturing practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market package rate for WFOE incorporation and Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, typically USD 2,000-4,000

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), including Articles 1 to 7, 18, 128, 154, 156, 172, 193 and 387, together with the Foreign Investment Act, Articles 1 to 10, and the Regulations on Permission for Investment in Taiwan by Foreign Investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), with the Investment Commission of the MOEA acting as the preliminary authority for foreign investment approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foreign Investment Application, Company Registration Application, and Articles of Incorporation (Charter) of the Taiwan Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-in capital applies under the Company Act of Taiwan. Nevertheless, the Investment Commission will review the adequacy of proposed capital relative to the manufacturing scope, and the subscribed capital must be remitted in foreign currency and converted into New Taiwan dollars in a Taiwan bank account before registration. No blocked escrow account is required; a bank capital certificate must be obtained and filed with the registration authority.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS, the undersigned shareholder(s) have formed a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (the Company) under the Company Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), with liability limited to the subscribed capital, and have selected the business scope of manufacture and aseptic tubing of ambient quick-cook tapioca pearls, including canned boba products, corresponding to ISIC 1030; and WHEREAS, the initial share capital of the Company has been subscribed as set forth in the Articles of Incorporation and all conditions precedent to incorporation have been satisfied or will be satisfied before filing; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, AS FOLLOWS: 1. That the subscription of the authorized capital is accepted, and the Board adopts the share subscription schedule representing one hundred percent of the issued and outstanding capital of the Company. The Chairman or Managing Director is directed to open a bank account in the Company name in Taiwan, to receive the foreign exchange capital remittance, to obtain the bank capital certificate, and to deposit the paid-in capital so as to enable the statutory registration of the Company. 2. That the registered office of the Company shall be established at the address set forth on the certificate of incorporation, and the Board hereby adopts such address as the statutory domicile for service of process, government notices, and corporate records. 3. That [name], holding [identification/passport number], is appointed as Chairman of the Board, [name] as General Manager, [name] as Corporate Secretary, and [name] as the responsible officer for tax, food safety, and environmental compliance, each to serve until the next annual shareholders meeting and until successors are duly elected and qualified. 4. That any two officers, one of whom must be the Chairman or General Manager, are authorized to sign all contracts, open bank accounts, execute funds transfer instructions, endorse instruments, and execute factory and office lease agreements. 5. That the Board approves the filing of the Foreign Investment Application, Company Registration Application, tax registration, food factory registration, environmental permits, and fire safety approvals, and authorizes counsel and officers to prepare, execute, and submit all necessary documents, and to make immaterial amendments subject to subsequent Board ratification. 6. That this resolution shall be effective immediately, and that a certified copy shall be delivered to banks, government authorities, counterparties, and other stakeholders as required. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all actions previously taken by the founding shareholder, officers, and counsel in connection with the formation, capital subscription, and preliminary licensing of the Company are hereby ratified, ratified, and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), through the online foreign investment application portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file a formal Foreign Investment Application identifying the proposed Taiwan WFOE, the parent company, the intended shareholding, the registered capital, and the business scope limited to manufacture and aseptic tubing of ambient quick-cook tapioca pearls and canned boba products. Include an investment and operational plan with expected factory location, production capacity, employment, and funding schedule. Attach notarized copies of the parent company certificate of incorporation and board resolution authorizing the Taiwan investment, together with a power of attorney to counsel. Upon review, the Investment Commission will check for negative-list exclusions and capital adequacy and will issue a Foreign Investment Approval Letter.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application form, signed by the foreign investor and proposed Taiwan directors
Notarized certificate of incorporation or business registration of the parent company
Notarized parent company board resolution approving the Taiwan investment
Draft Articles of Incorporation for the Taiwan WFOE
Investment plan, production plan, and preliminary factory lease or site information
Power of attorney in favor of local counsel or agent
Passport copies of proposed directors, shareholders, and statutory responsible officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or suspension, the applicant must submit supplementary explanations and documents within 15 business days, amend the investment plan or capital amount if required, and resubmit through the same portal. If the application is rejected, the investor may file an administrative appeal within 30 days under the Administrative Appeal Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Complete Initial Company Registration with the Department of Commerce, MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan (R.O.C.), via the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Online Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Foreign Investment Approval Letter, reserve the English and Chinese company name, then submit the Company Registration Application with executed Articles of Incorporation, the Investment Commission approval letter, the bank capital certificate, address and office consent, and appointments of directors, supervisors, and responsible officers. The Department of Commerce verifies the corporate name, legality of the business scope, capital, directors, registered office, and proposed governance structure. On approval, the Company receives the Company Registration Certificate and the Unified Business Number, which is the prerequisite for tax registration, banking, and licensing.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter issued by the Investment Commission
Executed Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital certificate showing deposit of paid-in capital
Registered office consent letter, lease, or proof of address authority
Letter of appointment or consent for each director, supervisor, and responsible officer
Company name reservation confirmation
Company Registration Application form
Authorized representative and counsel signatures and power of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA rejects or queries the registration because of name confusion, capital mismatch, or document defects, the applicant must cure the defects within 14 days by filing amended Articles or supplying corrected documents. A final denial may be contested by administrative appeal; no operations may commence until the Company Registration Certificate is lawfully issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Invoice, and Labor/Health Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Administration (NTA), Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (R.O.C.), and the Ministry of Labor insurance and health insurance administrative agencies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days after company registration, file for business tax registration, income withholding registration, and unified invoice, including the registration under the income tax authority responsible for the registered office. Simultaneously, register as an employer with the labor insurance and national health insurance system and submit the responsible officer identification and payroll policy. These steps activate the electronic invoice system and constitute the statutory tax and labor identification for hiring employees. The tax authority will issue a tax registration certificate and assign applicable tax types and filing dates.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number confirmation
Articles of Incorporation filed with MOEA
Registered office lease or ownership document
Photocopy of responsible person identification card or Alien Resident Certificate
Foreign Investment Approval Letter and bank account details
Employer registration forms for labor insurance and national health insurance
Unified invoice and electronic invoice registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTA issues a query for missing documents, the company must immediately submit the missing identification, lease, or charter documents. Late registration can be cured by filing with reasons for delay and requesting penalty abatement; payment of any assessed late fees must be made promptly to avoid continued suspension of invoice issuance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Food Factory Registration and Food Business Registration from TFDA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan (R.O.C.), and the local municipal health bureau with jurisdiction over the factory site.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before beginning commercial production, submit the Food Factory Registration application and Food Business Registration application covering the manufacture of canned boba tapioca pearls. Provide factory layout, production flow, water quality tests, hygiene control plans, HACCP or GMP program, product formula, ingredient specifications, label copy, lot tracing procedures, and thermal process or sterilization validation data for low-acid canned products. The TFDA or local health authority will perform an on-site sanitary audit and verify that the facility meets food safety, sanitation, and equipment standards. Upon approval, the authority issues the food factory registration number and food business registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Food Factory Registration application
Factory floor plan, equipment layout, and sanitary drainage plan
Manufacturing process flow and HACCP/GMP plan
Product formula, ingredient specifications, and label text
Thermal process / sterilization validation protocol for low-acid canned boba
Water quality test report and pest control records
Food safety responsible person certificate
Food Business Registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TFDA audit identifies nonconformities, the company must prepare a corrective action plan within 10 business days and request a re-inspection within 30 days. Production is prohibited until the Food Factory Registration is approved; a rejection may be remedied by revising the HACCP plan, sanitation procedures, or premises design and resubmitting a new application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Environmental Impact Assessment Determination and Environmental Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) of Taiwan (R.O.C.), with local municipal environmental protection bureaus handling discharge and fixed pollution-source permits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an EIA screening form to determine the applicable tier for the canned boba tapioca pearl factory. A conventional food canning facility will generally be classified as Category II Environmental Registration, requiring an environmental impact analysis and mitigation plan, while a facility located in a sensitive water-source, ecological, or high-pollution-load district may require a Category I Full Environmental Impact Assessment. After the tier determination, apply for a water pollution discharge permit, air pollution source permit, and waste disposal plan, submit quantitative wastewater, VOC, odor, and hazardous waste projections, and enter into approved treatment and transport contracts.
required_dossiers: EIA screening form and environmental tier classification request
Factory production capacity and process description
Wastewater discharge volume and quality projection with pretreatment facility design
Air emission inventory, VOC and odor abatement equipment specifications
Hazardous waste classification, storage, treatment, and disposal contracts
Noise, dust, and odor control plan
Waste Management Act registration and manifest forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EPA requires a full EIA or additional permits, the company must supplement the environmental report with additional baseline data and mitigation measures, or resubmit within 30 days. If feasible, the company may adjust production capacity, process design, or plant location to bring the project within a lower EIA tier, provided the change is legally permissible and approved by the authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure Civil Defense Fire Safety Approval and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Fire Bureau under the National Fire Agency, Ministry of the Interior, Taiwan (R.O.C.), and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Ministry of Labor.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the building fire safety design for review and install fire safety equipment in accordance with the Fire Services Act, including fire alarms, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and exits. Appoint a fire safety officer and file the fire safety management plan with the local Fire Bureau. For the manufacturing plant, obtain the building use permit and structural load inspection. Under occupational safety requirements, perform a workplace hazard assessment, appoint occupational safety staff, provide training records, and submit the workplace self-inspection plan to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Building Use Permit and structural load certificate
Fire safety design drawings and installation certifications
Fire safety management plan and fire safety officer appointment
Occupational hazard identification and risk assessment
Workplace preventive equipment list and employee training records
Occupational Safety and Health Administration registration forms
Emergency response and evacuation plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Bureau or labor inspector issues a violation notice, the company must immediately abate the fire or safety hazard, obtain a re-inspection date, and pay any penalties. Operations are prohibited if a red tag is issued; the company may cure by upgrading equipment, revising escape routes, or installing additional suppression systems within the period stated in the corrective notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Drug Administration (TFDA), Ministry of Health and Welfare, Taiwan (R.O.C.); Industrial Development Administration (IDA), Ministry of Economic Affairs; and local municipal health and environmental protection authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Factory Registration Certificate and Food Business Registration Certificate, together with the facility-specific Canned Food Low-Acid Thermal Process Registration where applicable for canned boba tapioca pearls.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA) of Taiwan (R.O.C.) and local municipal environmental protection bureaus.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Registration and Environmental Impact Analysis Report for conventional canned food manufacturing facilities; Category I - Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) required for facilities located in sensitive ecological, water-source, or high-pollution-load zones, or where the proposed scale exceeds the environmental determination thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Water pollution effluent standards under the Water Pollution Control Act: pH 6-9, 5-day biochemical oxygen demand not exceeding 30 mg/L, chemical oxygen demand not exceeding 100 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, and oil/grease not exceeding 10 mg/L. Air emissions: VOC abatement efficiency of at least 90 percent where abatement equipment is required, and no visible fugitive odor beyond the facility boundary. Hazardous waste: waste storage limited to 90 days, transport by a licensed hazardous waste carrier, and manifest reporting to the EPA on every shipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Management Certificate and Fire Safety Equipment Inspection from the local Fire Bureau under the Fire Services Act; Building Use Permit with structural load inspection; and occupational safety and health clearance from the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, Ministry of Labor, Taiwan (R.O.C.), including the approved workplace risk assessment, fire safety officer appointment, and emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; local competent tax service bureau at the WFOE's registered address; online portal: Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax) at etax.chinatax.gov.cn and the National Electronic Invoice Service Platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor does not obtain a separate Chinese TIN for the WFOE. Upon incorporation, the Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues the WFOE a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is legally the taxpayer identification number and VAT registration number. Procedure: (1) notarize and apostille/legalize the foreign parent's incorporation documents and board resolutions; (2) file the name pre-approval and foreign investment registration with SAMR; (3) obtain the WFOE business license with the USCC; (4) complete tax status registration through e-Tax within 30 days of the business license date, which also opens the VAT taxpayer file and consumption tax/social insurance links; (5) confirm VAT classification as small-scale or general taxpayer; (6) activate fapiao issuance through the STA electronic invoice platform. A foreign non-resident parent without a permanent establishment in China does not apply for a Chinese TIN; it uses its home-country TIN when claiming treaty benefits and when the WFOE withholds tax on dividends, interest, or royalties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity classification elections. The only relevant post-incorporation election is voluntary registration as a VAT general taxpayer for small-scale taxpayers whose annual taxable turnover is below CNY 5,000,000, which is a VAT compliance status election and does not change the entity-level CIT classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: All businesses with taxable activities must complete VAT registration. Mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable sales exceed CNY 5,000,000; below CNY 5,000,000 the taxpayer may remain a small-scale VAT taxpayer, while basic VAT registration is required from incorporation regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Fapiao issuance is mandatory. The WFOE must use the State Taxation Administration's National Electronic Invoice Service Platform under Golden Tax Project Phase IV, issuing VAT special invoices or fully digital electronic invoices with a unique invoice code, digital signature, and encrypted QR code transmitted to the STA at issuance in near real time. This enables nationwide tax clearance and cross-checking against customs, bank, and input invoice data. Traditional tax-control equipment is not used for fully digital e-invoice taxpayers; any private or ERP invoice arrangement must be interfaced to the STA-certified platform to have legal effect.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC Interim VAT Regulations and the export tax rebate (exemption, credit, refund) framework for exported goods, the WFOE, as a VAT general taxpayer and manufacturing exporter, may apply the 0% VAT rate to the export of canned boba tapioca pearls and claim a refund/credit of input VAT. Eligibility requires actual export from mainland China customs territory to Taiwan or another foreign customs territory; a completed customs export declaration; commercial export sales to an overseas buyer; receipt and repatriation of the export proceeds in foreign exchange within the statutory collection period; and submission of the export tax rebate declaration before the filing deadline. If the goods do not qualify for substantiated export zero-rating, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 13% output VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form (filed through the China International Trade Single Window, with customs release endorsement and export date)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill or international cargo manifest for non-ocean transport) evidencing physical departure from mainland China to Taiwan or another foreign destination

Bank-issued Export Proceeds Collection Statement (foreign exchange receipt/remittance advice, or SAFE Goods Trade Monitoring System record) proving the export payment was received and repatriated to the WFOE's PRC bank account within the collection period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA performs post-refund audits using Golden Tax Phase IV data to cross-check the customs export declaration, logistics documents, bank foreign exchange receipt, and VAT invoices. If the export zero-rating is not substantiated or proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day period, the refund is clawed back, the export is retroactively reclassified to 13% VAT, and late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day applies. Under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law, a false claim gives rise to a penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; fraudulent export tax refund claims also constitute the criminal offence of fraudulently obtaining export tax rebates under the PRC Criminal Law, punishable by fines of 1 to 5 times the defrauded amount, imprisonment up to life, and loss of export tax rebate qualification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed float and a strict separation between current and capital account items. Under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, RMB is fully convertible for bona fide current account transactions, including trade in goods and cross-border services, conditioned on genuine documentation and bank review. Capital account items, however, remain heavily controlled under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange registration framework. A Taiwan-invested WFOE manufacturing tapioca pearls may freely convert export proceeds into RMB, pay imported raw materials, and remit profits after tax, provided it files the relevant international income and expense declarations and presents invoices, customs declarations, contracts, and audited financials. The principal hurdles are the need for FDI foreign exchange registration before capital injection, supervision of capital account settlement by SAFE, denial of full capital account convertibility for speculative purposes, and strict documentary truthfulness checks. Profit remittance requires an audited PRC statutory report, tax completion certificate, and board resolution. Therefore, treasury design must route all cross-border flows through licensed bank counters and maintain a complete trade and capital KYC file.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Current PRC law does not impose a fixed mandatory conversion ratio. All export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated to China and either retained in a designated export foreign-exchange settlement account or converted to RMB at the WFOE's discretion. SAFE's total trade monitoring generally benchmarks export collection against the customs declaration within a 90-day post-export window; if collection is delayed beyond this window, the bank must flag the discrepancy and the WFOE must provide contracts, dispatch documents, and payment term evidence. The export proceeds from canned boba tapioca pearls and related goods may therefore be retained 100% in foreign currency or settled immediately.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational RMB Account, plus Export Receipts Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Capital Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable. PRC payment-institution regulations require any entity servicing RMB payments, foreign-exchange settlement, or cross-border trade payments for a domestically domiciled WFOE to hold a PRC payment license and be supervised by the People's Bank of China and SAFE. Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from opening domestic bank settlement accounts, handling capital account transactions, or performing FX conversion for a mainland-incorporated WFOE. The only compliant route is a licensed domestic tier-1 bank, with no reliance on foreign EMI banking rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative of the WFOE must attend a face-to-face KYC interview in the physical bank branch when opening the first basic deposit account; remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by PRC commercial banks for a new RMB basic account. If the legal representative is foreign, they must present the original passport and valid visa or residence permit. An authorized officer may accompany the legal representative, but the bank will usually require the legal representative's physical presence for the initial interview and signing of the account-opening resolution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to layered Taiwan and Hong Kong holding vehicles, creating unresolved controllers and round-tripping risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry search certificates for every vehicle in the ownership chain; full ownership chain to natural persons; notarized certificates of incorporation; audited financials and board resolutions; signed ultimate beneficial owner declarations; passport copies of all natural-person principals; and powers of attorney showing the authorised signatory chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering concern that canned tapioca is low-value and high-volume, allowing invoice over- or under-valuation between related Taiwan and PRC entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original commercial contracts and purchase orders; bills of lading and air waybills; customs export declarations; detailed packing lists and weight certificates; certificates of origin; transfer pricing documentation covering intercompany margins; and a transaction-by-transaction reconciliation of shipping documents to bank receipts and payments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and adverse-media listing triggered by Taiwanese shareholder names or trading counterparties appearing on PEP lists, sanctions lists, or negative news databases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed sanctions screening reports from provider-grade databases; official court and litigation search results in Taiwan and mainland China; passport and Taiwan ID certified copies; notarised statutory declarations covering source of wealth; media and public record review reports; and a PRC corporate credit report showing no enforcement or tax violations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection mismatch where proposed registered capital is disproportionate to the tapioca manufacturing operating cost base, or where funds arrive from a high-risk intermediary jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Projected cash flow and capital expenditure model; board resolution approving the capital increase; source-of-wealth evidence including shareholder tax returns and audited financial statements; bank reference letters from the remitting bank; SAFE FDI registration form; and a written explanation of every funding leg together with the intermediary bank name and payment reference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound investment capital must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan shareholder to the WFOE's designated SAFE-registered Capital Account at a licensed PRC bank. The remittance must carry SAFE transaction purpose code 6011 for foreign-invested enterprise capital injection, and the bank must verify the FDI foreign-exchange registration number before crediting funds. After receipt, the WFOE submits a capital settlement request supported by invoices, contracts, and capex plan; the bank converts the foreign currency into RMB in the capital project RMB settlement account. A licensed PRC CPA must then issue a capital verification report confirming that the paid-in capital is consistent with the registered capital and the audited financial statements.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For import of tapioca starch, sugar, flavoring, and packaging materials, the WFOE makes outward settlement by SWIFT MT103 after presenting the import contract, commercial invoice, customs declaration, and shipping documents to the bank. For larger or longer-tenor purchases, the WFOE can open an irrevocable commercial letter of credit through SWIFT MT700/MT701, with presentation of bills of lading, inspection certificates, and other compliant documents. Documentary collections (documents against payment and documents against acceptance) are usable for trusted counterparties. All disbursements must be matched to underlying customs declarations under SAFE goods-trade monitoring; any unmatched or overdue settlement may trigger an enterprise downgrade to B or C status.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD forward contracts with a licensed PRC bank, supported by genuine export or import exposure from tapioca pearl sales or raw material purchases
CNY/USD FX swaps for converting trade receipts and import payments across different settlement cycles, subject to underlying trade documentation
Bought FX options on USD/CNY to cap conversion cost, with covered risk-reversal structures only where the WFOE retains physical trade exposure
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term foreign-currency debt, with SAFE registration and underlying investment or trade finance validation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not permissible onshore for a PRC-domiciled WFOE; any NDF alternative may only be transacted by a legally separate offshore parent, not the mainland entity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 May of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end for calendar-year filers; e.g., FY2024 return due 31 May 2025; an automatic two-week grace period applies for e-filing; instalment plans for large enterprises file via prescribed schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: penalty of 3% of defaulted tax per each 2-month period, up to 9% maximum; late payment: interest at 1.28% per annum compounded for every 2 months plus an additional 10% to 15% surcharge on the unpaid balance; continued non-compliance triggers administrative sequestration, forced collection, business operation suspension notice, and ultimately a court-ordered dissolution and administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited or Reviewed Financial Statements and Business Report after Shareholders Approve
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Registration Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual general meeting must be held within six months of fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year company); the approved financial statements must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after shareholder approval, normally by 15 July of the succeeding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to register the financial statements within 15 days subjects responsible directors to a fine of NT$100,000-NT$500,000; repeated or material non-compliance can lead to MOEA compulsory correction, denial of future registration applications, and a petition to the court for dissolution of the WFOE

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Business and Shareholding Report (WFOE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (by 31 March for calendar-year company); the report must cover business operations, shareholder/beneficial owner structure, and if applicable, audited financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual report may result in a fine of NT$60,000-NT$300,000 under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals; the Investment Commission may suspend processing of any foreign-investment application, restrict repatriation of capital or earnings, and administrative registration of the WFOE may be revoked for persistent non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Food Factory Registration and Annual Sanitation Self-Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) / Local Health Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual sanitation self-inspection and declaration due by 31 January of the following year; the food factory registration itself requires renewal every 5 years from the original registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or defective sanitation declaration: administrative fine of NT$30,000-NT$300,000 under the Act Governing Food Safety and Sanitation; operating an expired registration leads to immediate production suspension, mandatory product recall, and possible criminal liability for responsible officers; repeated violations cause cancellation of the food factory registration and closure of the plant

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Business Tax (Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax) Filing and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (VAT District)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Four mandatory quarterly filings: Q1 due 15 April; Q2 due 15 July; Q3 due 15 October; Q4 due 15 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty: 1% per 2 days of delay on the unpaid tax; intentional under-remission or failure to file after official warning triggers surcharge of 15% of the total owed, plus an altered assessment based on official inspection; prolonged delinquency may lead to bank account freeze, attachment of company assets, and an administrative strike-off template for corporate dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Taiwan's Business Entity Accounting Act and the Regulations Governing Financial Statement Attestation by CPAs, a mandatory independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit is legally triggered for a WFOE if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded at the most recent fiscal year-end: (i) paid-in capital over NT$30 million (approx. USD 1,000,000); (ii) total annual net operating revenue over NT$100 million (approx. USD 3,333,333); (iii) total balance-sheet assets over NT$300 million (approx. USD 10,000,000); or (iv) headcount of more than 100 employees. In addition, a CPA-audited financial statement is mandated when required by the Investment Commission as part of the annual foreign-investment report, for all public companies, and for any enterprise seeking commercial bank credit exceeding statutory thresholds under financial regulator directives. Failure to appoint a licensed CPA when any threshold is triggered constitutes a violation punishable by fines of NT$120,000-NT$600,000 and by legal disqualification of independently prepared financial statements for tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS 2024 as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and the Accounting Research and Development Foundation (ARDF) for public companies; non-public WFOEs may elect to apply the Taiwan SME Accounting Standards (SME GAAP) or full IFRS consistently. All financial statements must be prepared in New Taiwan dollars and, when audited, must comply with Taiwan Statements on Auditing Standards (TSAS) issued by the ARDF. The Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax return requires reconciliation of statutory accounting profit to taxable income using the Business Entity Accounting Act and related tax rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act and the Company Act, the WFOE must maintain a Beneficial Ownership (UBO) register identifying any natural person with direct or indirect control of more than 25% of shares or voting rights. The UBO register must be updated within 30 days of any shareholding transfer, change of director, or other control event. Annually, no later than the date of the Annual General Meeting and prior to filing the Annual Foreign Investment Report (by 31 March), directors must certify the UBO register and submit a beneficial ownership schedule to the Investment Commission. The UBO register must be available for on-site inspection by MOEA, TFDA, and AML supervisory bodies; a separate statutory register of members, directors, charges, and minutes must be maintained at the registered office and updated promptly with any corporate resolution or board decision.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Transfer Ledger and Share Certificate Issuance Record

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% preferential rate for qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises; phased-in Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential rates reducing the effective rate to 5% for taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million; 100% additional deduction for eligible research and development expenses; exemption for qualifying technology transfer income up to RMB 5 million; and reduced final withholding tax rates available under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement for Taiwan-resident beneficial owners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000 of the A-Class Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return) and supporting schedules, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau portal (e-Tax platform).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return and final settlement are due within five months after the end of the tax year, i.e. by 31 May of the following calendar year; quarterly provisional enterprise income tax returns are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from sales of canned boba tapioca pearls, including export sales to Taiwan and other foreign markets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all operating revenue, including shipments to the Taiwan parent or affiliated distributors. Reconcile revenue with customs declarations and commercial invoices; adjust for arm's length pricing if the transaction is with a related party. Transfer pricing adjustments made by the tax authority must be reflected in Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Costs of raw tapioca starch, sugar, flavorings, packaging materials, aseptic tubing consumables, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only arm's length costs. Intercompany raw material purchases from Taiwan or other affiliates must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and must be valued under the Comparable Uncontrolled Price or Cost Plus method where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3: Business Taxes and Surcharges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: City maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and local education surcharges levied on actual VAT paid, plus other deductible taxes and fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident related party transactions do not reduce VAT surcharges. Export of canned boba tapioca pearls is generally zero-rated for VAT, so any export-related refunds and rebates must be reconciled in this box and in the VAT return to avoid inconsistent box-to-box treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Export freight, shipping insurance, overseas sales commissions, marketing expenses, and distribution channel costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Commission or marketing fees paid to a Taiwan-based affiliated distributor must be tested for business purpose and arm's length nature. The tax authority may disallow fees that duplicate services already performed by WFOE employees in China. Any fee paid to a non-resident is also subject to withholding tax analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5: General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Salaries, rent, professional fees, royalties, management fees, and other general overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties paid to the Taiwan parent for tapioca processing technology are deductible only if the technology is genuine, the fee is arm's length, and the WFOE can prove that it has not previously been compensated through inflated raw material prices. Management fees must be supported by actual services, and the Taiwan recipient remains subject to withholding tax unless treaty relief is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest on bank loans and shareholder loans, banking charges, foreign exchange losses, and other financing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For loans from the Taiwan parent or affiliated lenders, apply the thin capitalization rule: deductible interest is limited to a debt-to-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises. Interest paid to Taiwan lenders is subject to statutory 10% withholding tax, reducible to 7% under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement if a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership evidence are submitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated as Box 1 less Boxes 2 through 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the operating profit margin of the WFOE is significantly lower than comparable boba food manufacturers, tax authorities may invoke the Transactional Net Margin Method to adjust profit, especially where the Taiwan affiliate captures excessive residual profit. The WFOE must retain benchmark data supporting its gross margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit adjusted for non-operating income and non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any deemed dividend, debt forgiveness income, or recharacterized profit adjustments arising from a tax audit. Dividend distributions to the Taiwan parent are not deductible in this box and are dealt with through the separate non-resident dividend withholding declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit after tax-exempt income, loss carryforwards, and tax adjustments per Schedule A105000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only eligible losses may be carried forward five years; no carryback is permitted. Losses arising from a Taiwan branch cannot reduce mainland taxable income. Any excessive related-party interest disallowed by thin capitalization must be added back in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 / Line 14: Income Tax Payable at 25%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enterprise income tax computed at the statutory 25% rate on taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 15% High and New Technology Enterprise rate only if the WFOE holds a valid HNTE certificate for the tax year. Small Low-Profit Enterprise relief applies only to qualifying domestic enterprises; the Taiwan parent cannot claim the preferential rate directly. Foreign tax credits for Taiwan-sourced income may be claimed only with proper evidence of Taiwan tax paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 / Line 15: Final Tax Due after Prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable less quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits, resulting in a balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After filing, if the WFOE distributes profits to the Taiwan parent, the WFOE must separately withhold and remit dividend withholding tax within seven days of the withholding date. The A100000 filing itself does not remit the dividend withholding tax; use the non-resident enterprise withholding return and payment portal.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Non-Resident Supplementary Disclosure Schedule: Related Party Transaction Reporting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annual declaration of related party relationships and related party transactions under SAT requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the Taiwan shareholder, all intercompany purchases of tapioca ingredients, royalty payments, management fees, loans, and guarantees. Attach the Chinese version of the related party transaction form and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation when thresholds are exceeded. Failure to disclose is itself an independent compliance violation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts a fine of up to RMB 2,000, or up to RMB 10,000 for serious cases, plus a daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax. Under the Tax Collection Administration Law, understating tax through false returns triggers recovery of the underpaid tax, a daily surcharge, and an administrative penalty of 50% to 5 times the underpaid amount. If underpaid taxes are relatively large and exceed 10% of the amount of tax due, the taxpayer and responsible directors may face criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to three years for relatively large amounts and up to seven years where the amount is huge and exceeds 30% of total tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before any dividend payment to the Taiwan parent, the WFOE as withholding agent must file the non-resident treaty benefit application in accordance with SAT Announcement 2015 No. 60. The Taiwan shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from the Taiwan competent tax authority, provide a Beneficial Ownership Declaration, evidence of direct shareholding of at least 25% if the reduced 5% dividend rate is sought, and financial records proving the shareholder is not a conduit or mailbox entity. The application must be made before the dividend payment date; if the tax authority disallows treaty relief, the WFOE must withhold at the statutory 10% and remit within seven days. If relief is approved after withholding, a refund or offset may be pursued through the competent authority process under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax rates are 10% for outbound interest and royalties, and 10% for outbound dividends. Under the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement, interest and royalties paid to Taiwan-resident beneficial owners may be reduced to 7%, while dividends may be reduced to 5% where the Taiwan-resident beneficial owner is a company holding at least 25% of the WFOE capital, otherwise the dividend rate remains 10%. For royalties on canned boba technology and trademarks, the WFOE must also consider value added tax on imported services and the applicable surcharges, while interest paid to Taiwan lenders must be supported by formal loan agreements and arm's length interest rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is required when aggregate related party transactions in a tax year exceed RMB 1 billion. Local File is required when tangible asset transfers with related parties exceed RMB 200 million, financial asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, intangible asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, or other related party transactions exceed RMB 40 million. Related party transaction reporting schedules must be filed even below these thresholds whenever any related party transaction exists.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although the PRC does not apply the offshore Economic Substance Regulations model, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, together with the Special Tax Adjustment Measures, requires the WFOE to demonstrate actual commercial substance and core income-generating activities in China. For canned boba tapioca pearls, CIGA includes procurement of raw tapioca, formula ownership, aseptic manufacturing, quality control, inventory risk, invoicing, treasury decisions, and operational management. A WFOE with no manufacturing plant, no staff in China, and board decisions made entirely in Taiwan can be recharacterized as a shell; profits may be adjusted, deemed dividends may be taxed, and the Taiwan parent may be denied treaty benefits for lack of beneficial ownership.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE sells canned boba tapioca pearls to a Taiwan affiliate at below-cost prices while paying excessive royalties and management fees for a purported tapioca formula that lacks substantive technical support, and fails to prepare Local File or Master File despite related party transactions exceeding PRC thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 41 and Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, the tax authority may adjust related party pricing, recharacterize excessive royalties and fees as distributions, disallow interest deductions under thin capitalization, impose special tax adjustment interest, and apply Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, resulting in recovery of unpaid tax, daily interest at 0.05%, and an administrative fine of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly implement the profit-stripping arrangement face personal civil liability for the WFOE's unpaid tax and penalties to the extent that the corporate veil is pierced for abuse of limited liability. Directors may be placed on the tax authority blacklist, subjected to travel bans through the exit-entry control system, have personal bank accounts and assets frozen, and if the underpaid tax is relatively large and exceeds 10% of the total tax due, directors may be prosecuted under Article 201 of the Criminal Law for tax evasion with imprisonment from three to seven years for huge amounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False Export Invoicing, Export VAT Rebate Fraud, and AML Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE fabricates export orders for canned boba tapioca pearls to a shell buyer in Taiwan or Hong Kong, obtains false VAT special invoices, claims export tax refunds and cost deductions on the CIT return, and receives the proceeds through unofficial underground remittance channels, creating a false profit and evasion trail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: This triggers Article 204 and Article 205 of the Criminal Law for fraudulent export tax refunds and issuance of false special VAT invoices, with fines and imprisonment up to life imprisonment for severe amounts. Under the Tax Collection Administration Law and Anti-Money Laundering Law, the tax authority and customs bureau can recover the fraudulently obtained refund, impose fines of 100% to 500% of the refunded amount, revoke export qualifications, and refer the case for criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false invoices, instruct staff to create fake bills of lading, or route proceeds through underground channels are personally exposed to criminal arrest, travel bans, and blacklisting. Personal assets derived from the fraudulent refunds and false invoicing may be confiscated. Directors may also face unlimited joint and several liability for the WFOE's fraudulent VAT/CIT liabilities where the corporate form is used as a vehicle for crime.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure and Absence of Economic Substance / Beneficial Ownership Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE is registered in China but has no physical factory, no employees, no raw material procurement, and no decision-making in China; all manufacturing is subcontracted to a Taiwan affiliate, all board meetings are held in Taiwan, and profits are immediately distributed to a Taiwan mailbox parent that is not the genuine beneficial owner of the shares.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the General Anti-Avoidance Rules, the tax authority may disregard the WFOE as a shell, recharacterize its transactions, impute taxable profits to the Chinese business operations, and deny the Cross-Strait Double Taxation Agreement relief. The resulting unpaid tax and deemed dividend withholding tax will attract the daily 0.05% surcharge and an administrative fine of 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; the taxpayer will also be listed as a major tax violation case in the public blacklist system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Article 23 of the PRC Company Law, shareholders and directors who abuse the independent status of the limited liability company and shareholder limited liability to evade debts are jointly and severally liable for the WFOE's obligations. Directors are subject to travel restrictions, blacklisting by the tax authority, seizure of personal assets, and if the shell structure is used to evade CIT or WHT knowingly, prosecution for tax evasion under Article 201 of the Criminal Law with imprisonment of up to seven years may follow.
